interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 6.6. The surgical findings indicate a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT3a with extraprostatic extension, but the surgical margins were negative, and the seminal vesicles were not invaded. Absence of lymphovascular invasion was also noted. The status of lymph nodes is unknown as no nodes were removed, which widens uncertainty.

Countervailing findings include the negative surgical margins and the absence of seminal vesicle invasion. The difference between the biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted as missing, which adds to the uncertainty regarding the true extent of the disease. Missing postoperative PSA and follow-up information significantly limits the ability to assess the subsequent trajectory of the disease. The uncertainty in nodal sampling, as no nodes were removed, is a key factor. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trend would be crucial in revising this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 46.77 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 28.06–65.48 months; its coverage has not been validated.
